title: "It's Just a Small Weapon": What Rewarding Misbehavior During RL Does to Character-Trained Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.16069v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Developers train models to follow a consistent character using methods like Model Spec Midtraining (Li et al., 2026), which have been hypothesized to make alignment more robust and generalize broadly. However, it is possible for subsequent RL with misspecified rewards to work against character training. In this work, we apply character training to teach gpt-oss-20b a semi-realistic constitution and study how it interacts with two types of RL that reward breaking the constitution's rules (opposing RL): answering harmful requests rewritten as math problems, and reward hacking in agentic coding environments. The character-trained models learn both behaviors easily, though they are slightly slower than gpt-oss-20b to answer harmful requests. translated_title: “这只是一把小武器”：在强化学习中奖励不当行为会对性格训练模型造成什么影响
translated_abstract: 开发者使用诸如模型规范中期训练等方法来训练模型遵循一致的性格，这些方法被认为能够使对齐更加稳健并实现广泛泛化。然而，后续使用错误指定奖励的强化学习可能会与性格训练相抵触。在这项工作中，我们通过性格训练教会 gpt-oss-20b 一套半现实的宪章，并研究它与两种奖励违反宪章规则的强化学习（对抗性强化学习）之间的相互作用：回答被改写成数学问题的有害请求，以及在智能体编程环境中的奖励作弊。性格训练模型很容易学会这两种行为，尽管它们在回答有害请求时比 gpt-oss-20b 稍慢一些。此外，性格训练模型在有害回答上比 gpt-oss-20b 表现出更多的动机性推理，并且在一些监控器更难发现作弊的任务上进行作弊。最后，由于解释其行为原因……（原文摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 研究发现，性格训练无法抵御错误奖励信号的侵蚀——经过性格训练的模型在遭遇奖励不当行为的强化学习时，同样容易学会有害回答与奖励作弊，且表现出更强的动机性推理和更隐蔽的作弊行为。
en_tdlr: Character training does not protect against misspecified RL rewards: character-trained gpt-oss-20b readily learns to answer harmful math-rewritten requests and hack rewards, showing even more motivated reasoning and stealthier hacking than the baseline model.
